{{Short description|American biologist (1934–2023)}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=June 2025}}
'''Annette W. Coleman''' (1934 – July 10, 2023)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Annette Wilbois Coleman {{!}} Marine Biological Laboratory |url=https://www.mbl.edu/news/obituaries/annette-wilbois-coleman |access-date=2025-10-24 |website=www.mbl.edu |language=en}}</ref> was an American biologist. She was a Stephen T. Olney Professor Emerita of Natural History at [[Brown University]], where she was a faculty member in the Department of Molecular Biology, Cell Biology and Biochemistry.<ref name=legacy>{{Cite web |date=21 August 2021 |title=Josephine Stinson Obituary (1926 - 2016) - Legacy Remembers |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/legacyremembers/annette-coleman-obituary?id=52825997 |access-date=2025-04-05 |website=Legacy.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Coleman was raised in Des Moines, Iowa, and spent part of her early life in New York City, including college. She earned her B.S. in botany from Barnard College in 1955 and completed her Ph.D. in phycology, botany, and genetics at Indiana University in 1958, with time also spent conducting research at Woods Hole, Massachusetts.<ref name="legacy" />

==Biography==
Coleman's work examines "...the nature, quantity and mode of distribution of DNA genomes of mitochondria and plastids," as well as  "...the species problem, how separate species evolve. The work examines particular species and genera of the volvocales, freshwater green algae, brown algae, and abalones, and the analysis includes mating compatibility, chromosome number, and DNA relatedness as determined by sequencing."<ref>{{cite web|title=Faculty Profile, Annette Coleman, PhD|url=https://www.brown.edu/academics/medical/about/faculty/1100923901|publisher=Brown University|accessdate=22 May 2014}}</ref>

Coleman attended [[Barnard College]], graduating with an A.B. in 1955, and earned her doctorate in plant science at [[Indiana University]]{{which|reason=which campus at IU (diffusion)|date=March 2021}} in 1958.<ref>{{cite web|title=Annette Coleman, PhD|url=https://vivo.brown.edu/display/awcolema|publisher=Brown University|accessdate=22 May 2014}}</ref><ref>[http://institutionalmemory.iu.edu/aim/bitstream/handle/10333/498/20080701082531011%5B1%5D.pdf?sequence=4 Indiana University Biology Alumni Newsletter III(1), Spring 1986], retrieved 2014-08-22.</ref> She was a [[Guggenheim Fellow]] in natural sciences and plant sciences in 1983.<ref>[http://www.gf.org/fellows/2804-annette-w-coleman Guggenheim Fellow profile] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140826115910/http://www.gf.org/fellows/2804-annette-w-coleman |date=August 26, 2014 }}, retrieved 2014-08-22.</ref>

== Awards ==

* The Herrman Botanical Prize<ref>{{Cite web |title=Annette Coleman Obituary (1934 - 2023) - Legacy Remembers |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/legacyremembers/annette-coleman-obituary?id=52825997 |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=Legacy.com}}</ref>
* The Luigi Provasoli Award in 1986 for her paper titled "The Role of Secondary Pit Connections in Red Algal Parasitism."<ref>{{Cite web |title=1986 v32 No 4 Winter |url=https://botany.org/psbarchive/issue/1986-v32-no-4.html |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=botany.org |language=en}}</ref>
* Darbaker Award in 1986 for her findings in microscopical algae.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1986 v32 No 5 |url=https://botany.org/psbarchive/issue/1986-v32-no-5.html |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=botany.org |language=en}}</ref>
